# Class 15 {.ct}

![](../graphics/REB_Logo.png){fig-alt="Reaction Engineering Basics Logo" fig-align="center" width="200"}

## BSTR Operation and Sizing Analysis {.cc}

Class 15 examines the use of the BSTR design equations to specify reactor size and inlet conditions. It also describes IVODEs containing an unknown initial value or constant and demonstrates how to solve them numerically.

## Learning Outcomes {.ch}

After completing Class 15 you should...

* Know the definition of coupled unknown and an implicit equation
* Understand
    * to solve a set of IVODEs that contain an unknown, uncomputable initial value or constant a second final value, in addition to the stopping criterion, is needed
    * an unknown, uncomputable initial value or constant appearing in a set of IVODEs can be linked to a final value using an implicit ATE.
    * to solve an implicit ATE for the unknown initial value or constant, the residual function provided to the ATE solver must call an IVODE solver internally
* Be able to
    * write an implicit ATE for calculating an unknown initial value or constant in IVODE design equations
    * numerically solve design equations consisting of coupled ATEs and IVODEs
